reference_title: UFC 4-023-03, Design of Buildings to Resist Progressive Collapse (DoD, dated 14 July 2009, as amended through Change 4, 10 June 2024)

sections.title: Chapter Overview
sections.summary: Material-specific steel requirements; Appendix E demonstrates them on a 4-story building. Composite portions use the other applicable material chapter.
sections.body: This chapter provides the specific requirements for designing a structural steel building to resist progressive collapse. Appendix E demonstrates the application of the structural steel design requirements for a 4-story building. If composite construction with other materials is employed, use the design guidance from the appropriate material chapter for those elements/portions.
key_points: Validated in part via Appendix E's Table E-3 (Table 3-4 LIF anchor)

sections.title: Material Properties for Structural Steel
sections.summary: Over-strength factors from ASCE 41 Table 9-3 -- not reprinted in this UFC.
sections.body: Apply the appropriate over-strength factors to the calculation of the design strengths for both Tie Forces and the Alternate Path method. The over-strength factors are provided in ASCE 41 Table 9-3, Factors to Translate Lower-Bound Steel Properties to Expected Strength Steel Properties.
sections.applicability: Feeds QCE determination for steel Tie Force and Alternate Path calculations.

sections.title: Strength Reduction Factor Phi for Structural Steel
sections.summary: Phi comes from AISC 360, by component/limit state.
sections.body: For Alternate Path and Tie Force methods, use the appropriate strength reduction factor Phi specified in ANSI/AISC 360 Specifications for Structural Steel Buildings for the component and behavior under consideration. If steel components can be proven capable of carrying the required tie strengths while undergoing 0.20-rad rotation, use the appropriate Phi for each limit state considered.

sections.title: Tie Force Requirements for Steel
sections.summary: Apply the material-independent Section 3-1 Tie Force method for framed steel buildings; no steel-specific modification is printed.
sections.body: Apply the Tie Force requirements in Section 3-1, where applicable, for framed steel buildings.
key_points: Pure pointer to Section 3-1, no steel-specific modification

sections.title: Alternate Path Method for Steel
sections.summary: General procedure per Section 3-2 (5-4.1); beam and beam-to-column connection strength/rotational capacity per ASCE 41 as modified by 5-4.3 (5-4.2).
sections.body: General (5-4.1): use the Alternate Path method in Section 3-2, where applicable, to verify that the structure can bridge over removed elements. Connection Rotational Capacity (5-4.2): the design strength and rotational capacities of beams and beam-to-column connections shall be determined per ASCE 41, as modified by the acceptance criteria in Paragraph 5-4.3.
key_points: Connection capacities: ASCE 41 as modified by Section 5-4.3
sections.applicability: The steel-specific application of the general Alternate Path method.

sections.title: Modeling and Acceptance Criteria for Structural Steel
sections.summary: Use ASCE 41 Chapter 9 Life-Safety criteria generally, EXCEPT: (1) beams in flexure or flexure+axial-tension use Collapse Prevention values, (2) columns with P/PCL>0.5 are force-controlled with a P-M interaction cap of unity, and (3) the FR/PR connections listed in this UFC's OWN Tables 5-1/5-2 use those printed values instead of ASCE 41 Tables 9-5/9-6/9-7.
sections.body: With the exception of the connections and elements discussed below, use the modeling parameters, nonlinear acceptance criteria and linear m-factors for the Life Safety condition from ASCE 41 Chapter 9 for primary and secondary components; use ASCE 41's modeling parameters and guidance for the analytical model. Columns under high axial load (P/PCL > 0.5) shall be considered force-controlled, with P and M taken at their maximum analysis values and the P-M interaction equation not exceeding unity; for P/PCL <= 0.5, use the interaction equation with M as deformation-controlled and P as force-controlled. Nonlinear and linear acceptance criteria shall meet the Life Safety values of ASCE 41 Tables 9-5, 9-6, and 9-7, EXCEPT: (1) beams subjected to flexure or flexure-plus-axial-tension use Collapse Prevention values for primary and secondary elements, and (2) the Fully/Partially Restrained connections listed in this UFC's Tables 5-1/5-2 use the values given there. For the Double Angles PR connection, expected flexural strength is determined for each of the three listed limit states by accepted analytical procedures; for the Simple Shear Tab, expected flexural strength is the smallest strength from limit-state analysis (bolt shear, weld failure, block shear, bearing, plate flexure, etc.).
key_points: P/PCL>0.5 columns: force-controlled, P-M interaction capped at unity
P/PCL<=0.5 columns: M deformation-controlled, P force-controlled
Beams in flexure/flexure+tension: use Collapse Prevention (not Life Safety) values
Tables 5-1/5-2 (this UFC's own) replace ASCE 41 Tables 9-5/9-6/9-7 for the listed FR/PR connection types

sections.title: Enhanced Local Resistance Requirements for Steel
sections.summary: Apply Section 3-3's material-independent ELR procedure to framed and load-bearing wall steel buildings.
sections.body: Apply the Enhanced Local Resistance requirements in Section 3-3, where applicable, for framed and load-bearing wall steel buildings.
key_points: ELR for steel: pure pointer to Section 3-3
sections.applicability: Steel ELR design, validated in part by Appendix E.
